audit.why: 59.41% over 101 games, identical in both sources, and FAV at 4/10 is right. The mirror file audits/top/kassadin__sejuani.json reaches the same conclusion from his side and calls it a hard lane rather than a hard matchup, because Sejuani is a tank with no scaling once he reaches Riftwalk cadence. Both pages now say the same thing.

Sejuani for levels 1 through 5, Skill at Level 6, Skill at First item, Kassadin at Two-plus items. audit.whatIsWrong: Two separate factual errors, each repeated. First, six fields call Null Sphere a silence — whys[1], whys[2], spikes[0], early, wants.you[1] and wants.foe[0] all build advice on 'his Q silence'. Riot's Null Sphere text is 'fires an orb of void energy at a target, dealing damage and interrupting channels'. It does not silence. Second, whys[0] says his passive shield is 'irrelevant to your Frost stack damage' and early says his shield 'only blocks magic damage — your physical-adjacent frost damage pattern ignores it entirely'. Void Stone is not a shield, it is flat magic damage reduction ('Kassadin takes reduced magic damage and ignores unit collision'), and the magic shield lives on Null Sphere.
audit.why: The second error is the damaging one and it is backwards. Winter's Wrath, Permafrost and the Fury of the North shatter are all magic damage, so Void Stone's magic reduction plus Null Sphere's magic shield are the two most relevant defences he owns against her — not irrelevant ones. A Sejuani told her damage type ignores his passive will expect a kill that does not arrive. The mirror audit corrected the same silence claim from his side, so both pages now agree.
audit.corrected: The silence is replaced with the channel interrupt throughout whys[1], whys[2], spikes[0], early, wants.you[1] and wants.foe[0]. whys[0] and early now state that Void Stone reduces magic damage and Null Sphere shields magic, and that Sejuani's damage is magic.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid and loading tell the player to track Riftwalk and commit when it is down, with no number given anywhere.
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5 seconds at rank 1 and only 2 at rank 3, so it is never meaningfully 'down' — what actually gates it is mana, which is exactly what the page's own advice about watching his mana bar is groping toward. Telling a player to wait for a 2-second cooldown is telling them to wait forever. Force Pulse, by contrast, is 21 seconds at rank 1, and it is a slow, which Frost Armor makes her immune to.
audit.corrected: Riftwalk's 5-to-2-second cooldown and the mana-not-cooldown point are now in mid, breakdown.cooldowns and loading; Force Pulse's 21s and the slow immunity are in wants.foe[1] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The shatter half of Fury of the North is never stated on this page.
audit.why: Riot: 'Sejuani can damage a stunned enemy to shatter it, dealing massive magic damage.' Against the squishiest melee in the lane that is the whole reason the level-3 chain kills, and the mirror audit put the same fact on his page as the thing he must never let happen.

edits.before: Kassadin at level 1 is one of the squishiest melees in the top lane and his passive shield only blocks magic damage — your physical-adjacent frost damage pattern ignores it entirely. Take W at level 1, apply Frost stacks with the double-strike on every step-up, and walk. At level 2 your Q is live: if he tries to last-hit in the center of the wave, Q through him, let the knockup clear his Q shield window, and disengage before he silences you. Level 3 is your first real kill window — Q in, both W strikes to load Frost, E to stun him, finish the second W arc, walk. His Q silence cannot stop the E stun once stacks are already applied.
edits.after: Kassadin at level 1 is one of the squishiest melees in the top lane, but do not expect free damage: Void Stone reduces magic damage and Winter's Wrath, Permafrost and your shatter are all magic. Take W, apply Frost on every step-up, and walk. At level 2 your Q is live — if he last-hits in the middle of the wave, charge through him. Null Sphere interrupts channels and does not silence, so it cannot stop your W or E. Level 3 is your first kill window: Q in, both W strikes to load Frost, E to stun, and the shatter on a stunned target does massive magic damage. Finish the second arc and walk.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are still yours on paper but watch his mana bar — a low-mana Kassadin cannot Riftwalk out of your Q initiation, which means the full combo is free. A full-mana Kassadin can blink through your Q dash and leave you stranded, so track it before committing. At level 6 the dynamic shifts sharply in your favor: Glacial Prison is faster than his pre-items Riftwalk and travels far enough to catch him in the fog of the river. Coordinate with your jungler here — one Glacial Prison landing equals a stunned, silenceless Kassadin with no blink for three seconds. Every scuttle fight, every gank, every push-and-dive is now a potential kill.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are still yours, but track mana rather than cooldowns — Riftwalk is 5 seconds at rank 1 and 2 at rank 3, so it is never actually down; what stops him blinking out of your Q initiation is an empty bar. A full-mana Kassadin blinks through the charge and strands you, so check it before committing. At level 6 the dynamic sharpens in your favour: Glacial Prison throws 1300 and catches him in river fog before he can react. Coordinate with your jungler — one landed bola is a stunned Kassadin with no blink, and damaging him while stunned shatters Frost for heavy magic damage. Every scuttle fight and every gank is now a kill.

notes: Mirror reused: audits/top/kassadin__sejuani.json was already written and I took its findings rather than re-deriving them. The two directions now agree on the stage chart (Sejuani through Levels 4-5, Skill at 6 and First item, Kassadin at Two-plus items), on Null Sphere interrupting rather than silencing, and on Frost Armor's slow immunity versus Force Pulse. That mirror file flags two claims on the Kassadin page it could not verify — that Winter's Wrath deals a percentage of max HP, and that basic attacks feed Frost stacks. Riot's Winter's Wrath text mentions neither, and sejuani.json carries no percentHealth flag on W, but absence in the kit file means unknown rather than false. I did not assert either claim here and did not remove it there. Anyone with the live tooltip should settle both, since a max-HP W would change the trading maths on every Sejuani page, not just this one.
